title_ar: مرثية الشيخ الددو للشيخ الدين بن محمد علي ابن تكرور
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew’s Elegy for Shaykh al-Din ibn Muhammad Ali ibn Takrur
body_ar: أحقا نعيتَ الدين ذا الدين و الهدى و ذا العلم و الأخلاق و المجد و الندى و ذا السَّنن المرضي و السُّنن التي لها عن رسول الله قد كان مسندا ينافح عنها منكرا كل بدعة و ليس بهياب و لو كثر العدى و من حاز فينا السبق في الفهم و الذكا و من جاز فينا في مكارمه المدى و من أكسب الأجيال علمًا و سؤددا و عودهم من ذاك ما قد تعودا و من كان ندبًا مصقعا متصدرًا عزيزًا مكينًا في العشيرة سيدا نبيها نزيها لا يضام جنابه فعولا قؤولا للصواب مؤيدا لئن سار عنا الدين إثر رفاقه وخلف حزنًا في النفوس تبلدا فما مات من أبقى بنيه و آله و ما مات من أبقى ثناء مخلدا و صبرا بني موسى الكرام شيوخنا و سادتنا إنا لكم كلنا فدا فلا زلتم للدين و العلم مصدرًا و للجود و الأخلاق و العز موردا أحبتنا يا آل آمنة اصبروا فما الدين فيكم واحد بل تعددا بقيتم لنا كهفا و عزا و موئلًا و للدين و الأخلاق و العلم محتدا و أنزل ربي الدين أكرم منزل و أعطاه باليمني صحيفته غدا و أسكنه الفردوس جارا لجده رسول الهدى يا صدق ذلك مقعدا و بارك إلهي في بنيه و أمهم و بنتيه و احفظهم و أكرم و أسعدا و صل على خير الأنام و آله و أصحابه و التابعين ذوي الهدى
body_en:
[Verse. Rendered as prose, line by line; the Arabic is the operative text.]

*Is it truly al-Din whose death you have announced — he of religion and right guidance, of knowledge and character, of glory and open-handedness;*

*he of the well-pleasing way, and of those sunnah practices for which he held a chain of transmission going back to the Messenger of God;*

*defending them, repudiating every innovation in religion (bidʿah), and no faint-heart, however many the enemies grew;*

*he who among us took the lead in understanding and in quickness of mind, and who among us ran the whole course in his noble deeds;*

*who put knowledge and mastery into the hands of generations, and so accustomed them to it that it became their habit;*

*who was a ready man, eloquent of speech, foremost in place, honoured, firmly established, a chief among his clan,*

*high-minded, upright, his honour never to be slighted; a doer, a speaker, upholding what is right.*

*If al-Din has departed from us, following after his companions, and has left a numbing grief in our souls —*

*then he has not died who has left his sons and his household behind him, and he has not died who has left a praise that endures.*

*So take patience, noble sons of Musa, our shaykhs and our masters: may every one of us be your ransom.*

*May you never cease to be a wellspring of religion and knowledge, and a watering place of generosity, character and honour.*

*Our beloved ones, O house of Amina, be patient: al-Din among you is not one man — he is many.*

*You remain for us a cave of refuge, a strength and a haven, and for religion, character and knowledge a root stock.*

*May my Lord lodge al-Din in the noblest of lodgings, and place his record in his right hand tomorrow,*

*and settle him in the highest Garden as a neighbour to his forefather, the Messenger of guidance — how true a seat is that!*

*And may my God bless his sons and their mother, and his two daughters; and may He keep them, honour them and give them happiness.*

*And may He send blessings upon the best of mankind, and upon his family, his companions, and the rightly guided who followed them.*

flags.arabic: أحقا نعيتَ الدين ... فما الدين فيكم واحد بل تعددا
flags.context: the opening line and the twelfth line; the deceased is named al-Din
options: keep al-Din transliterated as a name and footnote the pun
render the name as "al-Din" but translate the second occurrence as "religion" where the sense demands it
render as "the Faith" throughout, keeping the double sense in English at the cost of the name
flags.note: The poem’s controlling device is that the dead man’s name is the word for religion, so that "you have announced the death of al-Din" says both "this man has died" and "religion has died" at once, and the consolation "al-Din among you is not one but many" answers it: the family has more men of that name, and more religion, than one death can take. No English rendering carries both. Option 0 is used and the device is explained here rather than resolved in the text.

flags.arabic: ذا السَّنن المرضي و السُّنن التي لها عن رسول الله قد كان مسندا
flags.context: the second line, in praise of the deceased
options: "he of the well-pleasing way, and of those sunnah practices for which he held a chain of transmission back to the Messenger of God"
"of the approved path and the sunnahs, for which he was an authority going back to the Messenger of God"
reading السَّنن as "the well-trodden road" and السُّنن as the legal category of sunnah acts
flags.note: The source vocalises the two words differently — السَّنن and السُّنن — marking them as a deliberate pair, but the two senses (a trodden path; the sunnah practices) are close enough that the distinction is hard to carry. مسند is likewise double: "one who supplies a chain of transmission" and "one relied upon". Option 0 takes the transmission sense, which fits a Shinqiti scholar’s praise; the alternative reading is recorded rather than discarded.

flags.arabic: و صبرا بني موسى الكرام ... أحبتنا يا آل آمنة اصبروا
options: two names for the same bereaved family, Banu Musa by the father’s line and Al Amina by the mother’s
two different groups being consoled in turn
آمنة as a place or clan name rather than a woman’s name
flags.note: The poem addresses بني موسى and آل آمنة within four lines of one another without saying how they are related. Mauritanian families are commonly named from either parent, which makes option 0 likely, but the text does not say so and the identification should come from the Sheikh’s office.

translator_notes: An elegy (marthiyah), not a fatwa. type is set to "article" for want of a verse type in the schema; the poem states no legal ruling and none has been inferred.
Rendered as prose line by line per style guide section 4; no rhymed English attempted, and the Arabic is retained as the operative text.

The deceased’s given name is الدين, al-Din, which is also the ordinary word for "religion". The poem turns on this throughout — most sharply in the opening (أحقا نعيتَ الدين, "is it truly al-Din / religion whose death you have announced?") and in فما الدين فيكم واحد بل تعددا, "al-Din among you is not one but many". The name is kept transliterated so the pun stays visible; see the flag.

جارا لجده رسول الهدى ("a neighbour to his forefather, the Messenger of guidance") implies descent from the Prophet. That is the poet’s claim about the family and has been translated as such, not asserted here.

The source writes باليمني for باليمنى ("in his right hand"), الذكا for الذكاء and العدى for الأعداء. The last two are ordinary poetic licence for the rhyme; the first is a spelling slip. All are preserved as found (style guide section 11).
